brief: JPM returns to a Tactically Bullish US equity view (first flagged a week earlier), citing a decline in October rate-hike odds from 64% to 22%, which pulled the 2Y yield to 4.82% from 4.85% and stabilized bond yields, alongside resilient macro data (ISM at 54.5, firm Dallas Fed), consumer strength despite a weaker September payroll print (3-month average ~51k, inside Feroli's 0-50k breakeven range), and improving technicals (seasonality, light positioning, retail participation). Q3 earnings growth is seen near 29% after 26Q2's 52%, which JPM flags as potentially light since all 11 sectors expect positive revenue and EPS growth. The Monetization Menu keeps Tech as a core long but drops the RTY short pairing on squeeze risk, prefers Banks over other cyclicals ex-AI, and names a US/Iran deal as the top catalyst for an EU/RTY squeeze. Separately, Marvell's investor-day guide-up (F28 revenue to $20bn; F31 Data Center revenue $67.5bn-$87.5bn) split the desk into bulls citing room to $30 EPS and bears questioning the long-dated targets and margins. France's Le Pen pledged €140bn in savings by 2032, helping French yields fall 10-11bp and lifting European equities.
